thread:
jamie: quick idea — propose we prune the tri-mode API surface and instead use a capability-first deployment manifest. move hosted/dedicated/private specific keys into a capabilities array (eg: ["kms-boundary", "dedicated-pool"]). reduces branching in control plane code and makes rollout semantics uniform. thoughts? :thinking:
sam: can you sketch what the new manifest looks like? less abstract pls.
jamie: sure, rough example:
```json
{
  "service": "redwood-model",
  "version": "v1",
  "capabilities": ["hosted-streaming", "kv-cache"],
  "billing_profile": "standard"
}
```
jamie: the idea: runtimes advertise capability requirements, control plane matches to capacity and policy; we stop having separate mode-specific code paths in the API layer.
lee: main concern is authz surface. hosted vs private have different identity proofs and claim flows. how do we ensure we don't weaken guarantees when we generalize?
taylor: also metering/billing differences — dedicated customers expect per-GPU reservations and different SLA metrics. will capability flags be expressive enough?
sam: could we do it incrementally? keep legacy fields, ingest them into capabilities on write, and add a compatibility flag so older control-plane components still work. deprecate after N months.
jamie: exactly — migration plan: 1) accept legacy keys and translate to capabilities on create/update 2) expose a read-only "legacy_mode" until deprecation 3) add opt-in strict validation for tenants who want the new model early. canary rollout.
lee: for authz, proposal: attach a small credential-type field to capability declarations (eg "kms-boundary:customer-kms") so the control plane still knows which KMS/arg is required. won't leak implementation details but keeps enforcement anchors.
taylor: billing: we need a mapping table in billing svc: capability -> billing meter + SLAs. ops can maintain mapping, and we can evolve mapping without changing manifests.
ops-bot: heads up: any migration that touches manifests will trigger audit events and may require data-migration quota checks. add an entries: ["migration:tri-mode-prune"] to the audit plan.
jamie: good call. i'll draft a short RFC with example transforms, migration script sketch, and canary rollout plan (5% tenants -> 20% -> full over 8 weeks). will include authz token flow for "kms-boundary" and billing mapping table. anyone want to co-author? :+1:
sam: I'll help with the transform script and tests.
lee: I'll write the authz section.
taylor: i'll do billing mapping and SLA test matrix.
jamie: awesome — i'll publish the RFC later today and ping infra/sre for the rollout checklist. thanks all. :rocket:
